Generate pipeline

Loading branch context...

Fill the fields below, then generate the pipeline. The generator will push the template, ensure the project Docker/Nginx DevOps repositories and starter files, register the YAML pipeline in \komodo, and create its classic Release definition. It will then show review links without running or redirecting to the Pipeline.

Extension authorization is required

Azure DevOps could not issue an extension access token. A Collection Administrator must authorize the Pipeline Generator scopes in Collection Settings → Extensions.

Authorize the requested scopes first. If no authorization action is shown, reinstall the same published version, then return to the target branch and run Generate pipeline again.
Captured from the branch list action. To change it, reopen the generator from the desired branch.
Use the build pool that will run the generated pipeline.
Lowercase identifier for the service being deployed. Auto-filled from the repository name when available.
Environment names and domains are loaded from ShonizCollection/SharedTemplates/SharedTemplates:/pipeline-generator.yml; the name is auto-detected from the branch when possible.
Enter the relative folder that holds your Dockerfile (for example: . or services/api). Override the default if auto-detection is unavailable.
Base registry address used by the generated pipeline template.
Azure DevOps service connection that provides credentials for the registry address above.
Loaded directly from Komodo using the central read-only credential file in ShonizCollection/SharedTemplates. Disabled servers are not shown.
Auto-generated from the project name using the exact casing (for example: ProjectName_Azure_DevOps). The extension will create or reuse this repository.

Review generated files before running the pipeline

The files are only starter templates. Review and edit them, then open and run the Pipeline once.
